articles.title: NSE's electronic gold receipts could generate ₹1,260 crore revenue by FY30, says Jefferies
articles.excerpt:
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) could generate nearly ₹1,260 crore in annual revenue from its Electronic Gold Receipts (EGR) business by FY30, if the platform develops into a large spot market for gold trading, according to estimates by global brokerage Jefferies.

The brokerage estimates that trading volumes on the platform could reach 18,750 tonnes by FY30, assuming volumes of 25 times India’s annual gold consumption. This would translate into a turnover of about ₹229 lakh crore.

articles.title: Silver futures decline to ₹1.85 lakh per kg
articles.excerpt:
In New York, silver was trading 2.59 per cent down at $50.80 per ounce | Photo Credit: MicroStockHub

Silver prices fell by ₹4,153 to ₹1,85,300 per kilogram in futures trade on Friday as participants reduced their bets.

On the Multi Commodity Exchange, silver contracts for December delivery declined by ₹4,153, or 2.19 per cent, to ₹1,85,300 per kg in a business turnover of 3,944 lots.

Analysts said a sell-off by participants mainly weighed on silver prices.

Globally, the white metal was trading 2.59 per cent down at $50.80 per ounce in New York.
